source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Confirm the cause of the incident. This is often caused by equipment failure.
3. Check the monitoring records before and after the incident. Ensure the issue was not long-lasting. If the incident lasted longer than 10 minutes, the Montgomery County Health Department will likely need to know about this. Do note the time of this incident in your report.
4. Check that the records show that the incident did not occur very often. Usually, one single incident is tolerated.
5. Fill out the TEQ.
6. Provide the detection limit for your monitoring. This TEQ is normally a minimum detection limit and not the lowest one possible that can be found. This needs to be as low as possible.
7. Make sure your monitoring data is not dependent on the concentration levels of the chemical being monitored (Note: continuous emissions monitoring systems are preferred because of this).
8. Have a cover letter describing the incident and the cause
